correctness.rationale: A weight-three binary BCH codeword corresponds bijectively to an unordered triple of distinct norm-one elements of F_{q^3} summing to zero; no weight one/two exists. Normalize one root to 1, reduce to x and 1+x in norm-one subgroup. For non-base-field x, its cubic minimal polynomial has coefficients a,b,1 and N(1+x)=a+b, hence b=a+1. The f_a(T)=T³+aT²+(a+1)T+1 family is reducible iff it has F_q root t∉{0,1}, forcing a=φ(t)=(t³+t+1)/(t²+t). The 3-cycle t→1/(1+t) preserves φ; its two fixed cube roots arise exactly when s even and correspond to distinct parameters. Thus irreducible cubics I=(2q+2)/3 (s odd) or (2q−2)/3 (s even); the norm-one intersection K=3I+2*1_even =2q+1−(−1)^s, with 2 extra base-field cube roots when even. Therefore A3=nK/6 and each coordinate incidence K/2=q+1 if odd, q if even. Independently computed φ image sizes over GF(4), GF(8), GF(16): 2,2,6; A3=28,219,1456, agreeing with theorem. Finite tests do not establish all-s orbit count.

originality.rationale: Qualified PASS: Wang et al. Theorem 12 establishes minimum distance three and uses exactly the same family f_a and φ to prove existence of irreducibility, but stops at the lower bound of at least one irreducible cubic. Exact number of irreducible f_a and total weight-three multiplicity requires the new order-three orbit argument; not identified in the original inspected relevant section. Older complete weight enumerators / Singer finite geometry might give equivalent formula.

value.rationale: A full exact first nonzero weight-enumerator coefficient and a parity-driven incidence design for a natural infinite family of distance-three binary BCH codes. The work meaningfully strengthens the known existence-based minimum-distance result by classifying every minimum-weight support, which matters for code-spectrum calculations.
